history.content: The appeal of free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channels has always been the way they make it easier to (re)discover classic films and series. But Roku’s latest experiment in the FAST space has less to do with traditionally produced entertainment and is entirely focused on giving viewers access to a constant source of AI-generated content.This week, Roku added four new channels to its library of streamable programming. Along with dedicated feeds for old episodes of Mad TV, Whose Line Is It Anyway?, and a variety of Black sitcoms, the platform also debuted a 24/7 stream filled with projects from Colin Petrie-Norris’ AI startup, Fairground. Partnering with Roku is a significant step up for Fairground, which launched in 2025 and is reportedly working on its own AI-generated adaptations of Robin Hood and Dracula. But watching the Fairground channel, you get the distinct sense that Roku hasn’t really gotten all that much out of the deal aside from the ability to say that it’s getting in on the gen AI craze.Like all FAST channels, Fairground AI Creator TV is filled with a curated selection of programming that you’re meant to watch somewhat passively. While you can scrub forward and backward a few seconds, there’s no way to choose exactly what kinds of videos the channel serves up. That might add a fun sense of discovery to the channel if it featured series and films that were actually riveting. But everything that I saw while watching for about an hour was more or less the same kind of short-form slop that text-to-video models have become known for.Aside from being produced with AI, there’s no consistent theme or genre to any of Fairground’s programming — all of which is made by a selection of content creators who have partnered with the company. Some videos are clearly generated by models trained on footage ripped from professionally produced anime, while others just look like terrible “lifelike” CGI. Surprisingly, there were semi-cohesive narratives to some of what I watched. I could follow what was going on in a “live-action” horror about people destroying a demon by making fun of it, and I got the sense that a fantasy about Greek heroes might have been inspired by The Odyssey.Image: Roku / FairgroundYou can tell from the videos’ length and the way their audio is mixed that there was some degree of post-production editing. But the videos’ general lack of visual polish makes it obvious that they were cobbled together from machine-generated clips rather than shots crafted by a human artist. And the overall shoddiness of Fairground’s programming becomes especially apparent whenever the stream cuts to an ad — this is a FAST channel — for one of the traditionally produced movies and shows Roku offers.Fairground’s website makes a point of emphasizing that it pays its content partners for their generations in addition to giving them an undisclosed share of the platform’s revenue. There’s no mention of which models are used to create Fairground’s content or whether it secured rights to use whatever training data is in the mix. But Fairground does stress that its programming is designed for “the living room, not the feed,” which says a lot about what kind of niche Petrie-Norris and his team are trying to carve out.RelatedPour one out for Roku CityAI slop movies are the new direct-to-video cash grabsIs paying artists enough to convince them to embrace AI?Most AI production startups have framed themselves as being poised to revolutionize the entertainment industry with technologies that will render traditional production workflows obsolete. Generally, the “Hollywood is so cooked” set insists that AI will soon be able to churn out films and shows comparable to a major studio’s, but that doesn’t really seem like the approach Fairground is leaning into. Rather than trying to be just as good or better than regular programming, it feels like Fairground simply wants its content to exist in the same general space as stuff that people might intentionally go looking for. Apparently, Roku thinks Fairground’s offerings are good enough to be platformed, which is depressing, but not altogether shocking as the company enters its Fox era.Fairgrounds’ content isn’t at all impressive, but its presence on Roku gives the startup a way to reach a massive audience of potential viewers. It’s easy to imagine an AI company seeing a business opportunity in the “looking for something mindless to play in the background” crowd, but this stuff doesn’t feel like something anyone would want to put on.

history.titleZh: Watching Roku’s AI channel is like eating from a trough
history.descriptionZh:
免费广告支持型流媒体电视（FAST）频道的一大卖点，在于它让观众更容易重新发现那些经典电影和剧集。然而，Roku最近在FAST领域进行的最新尝试，却与传统制作的娱乐内容关系不大，其核心是为观众提供源源不断的AI生成内容。本周，Roku在其可流媒体节目库中新增了四个频道：除了分别播放《Mad TV》老剧集、《Whose Line Is It Anyway?》以及多种黑人情景喜剧的专门频道外，平台还上线了一个24/7不间断播放的流媒体频道，内容全部来自Colin Petrie-Norris旗下AI初创公司Fairground的作品。

与Roku的合作对Fairground而言是一次重大跃升——这家公司于2025年成立，据报道正在开发基于AI生成的《罗宾汉》和《德古拉》改编作品。不过，实际观看Fairground频道后，你会明显感觉到，Roku这笔交易除了能对外宣称自己涉足了生成式AI热潮之外，似乎并没有获得太多实质性的好处。

和所有FAST频道一样，Fairground AI Creator TV提供的是经过策划的节目合集，适合观众被动观看。虽然你可以前后拖动几秒钟，但无法主动选择频道会播放哪种类型的视频。如果频道里播放的是真正扣人心弦的系列或电影，这种随机性或许能带来一种发现的乐趣。但在我观看的大约一小时里，所见内容几乎都是那种文本生成视频模型所特有的、千篇一律的“劣质短篇”（slop）。除了是AI制作的之外，Fairground的节目没有任何统一的主题或类型——所有内容都来自一批与公司合作的创作者。有些视频明显是由基于从专业动画中截取素材训练出的模型生成的，另一些则看起来像糟糕透顶的“逼真”CGI。令人意外的是，我看到的某些内容确实有半连贯的叙事。我能够看懂一部“真人”恐怖片中人们通过取笑恶魔来消灭它的情节，也感觉到一部关于希腊英雄的奇幻片可能受到了《奥德赛》的启发。

从视频的长度和混音方式可以看出，这些内容经过了某种程度的后期制作编辑。但视频整体缺乏视觉精细度，明显能看出它们是由机器生成的片段拼凑而成，而非由人类艺术家精心拍摄的镜头。Fairground节目的粗糙感在频道插入广告时尤为刺眼——毕竟这是FAST频道——与Roku提供的传统制作电影和剧集的广告相比，差距立现。

Fairground的网站特别强调，它除了付给内容合作方一笔固定报酬外，还给予他们平台收入中未披露比例的分成。网站没有提及使用哪些模型生成内容，也没有说明是否获得了所涉训练数据的使用权。不过，Fairground确实强调其节目是“为客厅设计，而非为信息流设计”，这充分说明了Petrie-Norris和他的团队试图开拓的细分市场。

大多数AI生产初创公司都把自己描绘成准备用技术彻底颠覆娱乐产业、让传统制作流程过时的力量。通常，“好莱坞已经完蛋”的那群人坚称，AI很快就能批量产出堪比大制片厂水平的电影和剧集。但这似乎并不是Fairground所采取的策略。它并没有试图与传统节目一样好或更好，而是感觉Fairground只是想让自己的内容存在于人们可能会主动寻找的同一类空间里。显然，Roku认为Fairground的内容足以被平台化，这令人沮丧，但考虑到公司正进入其“Fox时代”，倒也并不完全令人震惊。

Fairground的内容本身并不令人惊艳，但它在Roku上的存在，给了这家初创公司触达庞大潜在观众群的机会。很容易想象，有AI公司会在“想找点无脑内容当背景音”的人群中看到商机，但这样的东西给人的感觉是，似乎没人会真的愿意把它放出来看。
